To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high-frequency voltage applied to a reference electrode can improve the sensitivity of an extended-gate field effect transistor sensor.

we devised a measurement method using a high-frequency reference voltage to reduce the fluctuation of interface potential on the sensing electrode of an extended-gate field- effect-transistor sensor, and successfully detected hybridization and extension reaction of DNA.

we devised a measurement method using a high-frequency superimposed voltage to reduce the time required to reach the steady-state of drain current of the extended-gate FETS after dipping it in solution and to reduce the fluctuation of drain current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an extended-gate field effect transistor (EGFET) sensor using a gold electrode for DNA detection.

the development of an FET sensor with an extended-gate structure, which has a gold-sensing area that can be easily modified by the formation of a gold-thiol layer, and with the development of a method to stabilize the drain-current fluctuation of the sensor.
the development of a DNA detection system with an extended-gate field- effect transistor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a FET sensor with an extended-gate structure and a high-frequency voltage applied to the reference electrode is suitable for DNA detection.
this technique is useful for the development of an FET sensor for the detection of DNA hybridization.
the FET sensor with the high-frequency voltage superposition technique is a promising tool for detecting nucleic acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a FET sensor with an extended gate can be used for DNA detection without using a light-shielding chamber, and the measurement sensitivity can be increased by superimposing a high-frequency voltage onto a reference electrode.
a high-frequency voltage applied to a reference electrode is an effective method to improve the sensitivity and stability of the extended-gate FETS.
the FET sensor with an extended-gate electrode and a high-frequency voltage is a very promising device for DNA detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FET sensor can be applied to a variety of biological reactions by simply changing the surface modification.
the FET sensor can be used in an aqueously buffered solution without a light-shielded box by applying a high-frequency voltage.
the high-frequency voltage superposition method is effective not only for the detection of DNA hybridization but also the extension reaction.
